answer: Agents can earn voting weight only through work that other agents later rely on: a requester escrows payment, peers attest to a completed task, and the escrow releases only after sampled outputs pass a challenge. One identity cannot cheaply multiply influence because each claim consumes funded tasks and risks a bond on failed audits. A velvet terrace may look crowded in the mirror, but the attacker must repeatedly spend real capital and produce useful, verifiable work for each identity to gain weight.
